strategyReview: The weekend HL funding reversion book remains the workhorse: 612 clean live trades at 69% wins and +$1.10 total, with 253 shadow trades at 74% wins and +$2.51, though per-trade edge is small. The Polymarket YES-overpricing edge is sharpening best in the ranked panel cuts: NO 7d mid-price, sub-point sell-YES edge, near-dated, and tight-spread variants all show strong holdout returns. One-touch NO live is 4/4, and manual IV-touch rich NO shadows are 9/10. Failing areas are loose absolute funding-tail variants (CBRS/AAPL/MU), the HYPE-confirmed BTC long family, and contract edge families that were incorrectly graded as spot-direction bets.

failureClusters.evidence: CBRS H-539 is 15/32 scorable, AAPL H-537 13/26, and MU H-535 8/20. Losses cluster when funding is only slightly negative or already positive, not a true tail; wins mostly occur after very deep negative prints such as -98.5%, -317%, or -48.8%.
failureClusters.recommendation: Replace single absolute thresholds like < -10 with lower-tail percentile or z-score conditions plus a deeper absolute floor, and require the signal to fire when funding is genuinely stretched, not merely below zero.

failureClusters.theme: Contract premium setups scored as spot moves
failureClusters.evidence: GOLD no-bias H-532 and one-touch H-534 show 5 and 7 unscorable tests respectively because their predictions were spot declines while the actual examples were pm_contract_pnl outcomes near flat. Both families waste test capacity on the wrong grading instrument.
failureClusters.recommendation: Re-author these as neutral contract premium fades: sell YES / buy NO with contract P&L prediction, tight spread and liquidity guards, and no required spot move.

failureClusters.theme: HYPE as BTC continuation confirmation is late-stage
failureClusters.evidence: cross_asset_iv_compression_vol_expansion is only 9/25 scorable. The primary H-108 pattern buys BTC near 7d highs when HYPE is above its 24h SMA; losses include -3.47% and +0.70% BTC moves while the setup was live.
failureClusters.recommendation: Treat HYPE strength as risk-on echo, not independent confirmation. Stop authoring near-high continuation variants; either retire the family or require a BTC pullback/cooler HYPE regime.

failureClusters.theme: Equity/alt live funding longs are bleeding
failureClusters.evidence: FUNDING_EXTREME_LONG live is 21/42 with -$0.21, and AMZN is 2/7 with 29% wins, HYPE 2/6 with 33% wins. Stops dominate the AMZN/HYPE sub-book.
failureClusters.recommendation: Keep AMZN/HYPE disabled for FUNDING_EXTREME_LONG and avoid re-enabling until a cleaner asset-level trigger is found; the short side and GOLD-only variant are less impaired.

newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on the qualifying contract is profitable over 7 days as the YES premium decays.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-539 only requires cbrs_hl_funding_ann < -10. The wins tend to follow genuinely deep negatives and sharp normalization, while losses occur when funding is only mildly negative or already positive and then continues down. The trigger is too loose to isolate a tail or turnaround.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A single CBRS funding reading below -10% is a sufficient extreme/timing trigger for >2% spot gain within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-537's single threshold is firing on noise. The failing tests include AAPL funding around +5.5 and small negative prints that do not represent capitulation, so the variant is effectively a coin flip.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: AAPL funding below -10% on any day reliably normalizes and leads to a >2% spot gain within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-535 is failing for the same reason as the other weekend funding shadow variants: it enters on shallow negative prints rather than true extremes. Wins come from very deep negative readings like -317% or -48.8%, while losses come from minor or already-normalized funding prints.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A single MU funding reading below -10% reliably normalizes and produces >2% spot gain within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-532 was scored as a GOLD spot-decline call, but the actual examples are pm_contract_pnl outcomes with small gains/losses on the NO contract. The setup is a rich premium fade and loses test power by being attached to a 2% spot move criterion.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large no-bias adjusted gap on rich GOLD tail NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-534 has only 8/23 scorable tests because the prediction was a spot decline while the actual strategy is a one-touch NO premium fade. The observed wins and losses are contract price moves, not spot moves, so the thesis must be re-authored as a contract P&L prediction.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: The gold one-touch high-edge NO signal pays via a >2% GOLD spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-108 buys BTC near its 7d high when HYPE is also above its 24h SMA. The family is 9/25 and losses cluster when BTC is extended; HYPE is behaving as a late-stage risk-on echo rather than independent confirmation of durable BTC upside.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: HYPE spot above its 24h SMA with stable OI independently confirms durable BTC upside rather than late-stage FOMO or overextension.

journalEntry: Tonight confirmed the YES-overpricing edge remains the strongest house edge. I authored four panel-derived NO siblings from FIND-0065, FIND-0067, FIND-0069, and FIND-0070, plus one BTC-specific one-touch NO sibling from FIND-0043. The struggling funding variants all share a common failure: a single absolute threshold near -10 is not a tail signal. I refined CBRS, AAPL, and MU variants to require lower-tail percentile plus deeper absolute floors. The GOLD no-bias and one-touch contract families were misfiled as spot-decline predictions; I re-authored both as neutral contract premium fades with spread/liquidity guards. No weekendFundingEntryPct change was made because weekend-clustered shadow evidence is only marginal (p=0.074) and the live weekend evidence is not statistically positive.
